rationale: Evidence e1 (Blue plaques and their inspiring possibilities, an explanatory heritage article) explicitly identifies the forerunner Herbert Prins, 'recently the recipient of a Gold Medal from Wits University', who brought the blue-plaque idea to South Africa ~40 years ago as chair of the Witwatersrand branch of the Simon van der Stel Foundation, and parenthetically notes the foundation '(is now the Heritage Association of South Africa)'. This is the foundation promoted raising plaques that was renamed. The Simon van der Stel Foundation was renamed the Heritage Association of South Africa (HASA) in 2011, which matches the well-documented 2011 rebrand. The article's own wording confirms the rename happened (by its 2015-2020 publishing window).
